short_description: Gram-positive, strictly anaerobic, non-motile, non-sporing rod (2-5 um) that is characteristically BIFID - forked into a Y or club-ended branch, which is what gives the genus its name. One of the first colonisers of a newborn's gut, it ferments human milk oligosaccharides the baby cannot digest via the bifid shunt, and the acetate and lactate it releases acidify the gut and keep pathogens out.
colour_note: No pigment; a single cell is colourless and translucent (a plate of colonies is creamy-white, #F1E9DA). All colour in these plates is teaching convention, kept consistent across styles: cell body warm translucent cream, thick wall dusty ochre-olive, plasma membrane teal line, nucleoid blue-violet fibrils, ribosomes muted teal dots, exopolysaccharide a pale mint haze, pili fine ochre threads.
